A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, all 17 figures, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic and real-data network experiments in Section 5, including transfer learning in Figure 13, plus SST-5 and ImageNet feature analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including network comparisons, assumption validation, and transfer-learning outcomes.

M1.justification: The deep linear network formulation, MSE training objective, gradient-descent procedure, and feature-compression/discrimination framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic nearly orthogonal data, CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-100-to-CIFAR-10 transfer, and the Appendix B SST-5 and ImageNet analyses. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same linear, nonlinear MLP, and hybrid-network comparators. The projection-head configurations compared in Figure 13 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, architectures, initialization, optimizers, and training budgets are retained. Examples include the 400-epoch CIFAR-10 experiments in Section 5.1.1 and the 200-epoch pre-training and downstream probing phases in Section 5.3.2.

E4.justification: The depth, width, and initialization analyses, before/after-training comparisons, theoretical-bound checks, and projection-head-depth study are retained with the same evidence, including the supplementary analyses in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds for the depth/generalization experiments, ten runs with standard-deviation bars in Figure 7, and three-seed standard-deviation shading in Figure 13. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–17 retain the same plotted results, bounds, and uncertainty displays. The reported compression, discrimination, generalization, transfer-learning, SST-5, and ImageNet findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4's Assumptions 2–3 and Theorem 4 become v5's Assumptions 1–2 and Theorem 1. Definitions, mathematical bounds, and derivations in Appendices A and C are retained; corrected cross-reference labels do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric within-class compression, linear between-class discrimination, theoretical novelty, relevance to nonlinear networks, and transfer-learning implications.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same qualifications concerning data and weight assumptions, extrapolation to nonlinear networks, training difficulties with depth, and reduced transferability or out-of-distribution performance from excessive compression.

D1.justification: v5 adds a Project Page link in its front matter. The existing code-repository link remains available, and implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and data-processing disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained, including discussions of He and Su, Saxe et al., and Jacot et al. v5 replaces author-year citations with numbered references.

P1.justification: v5 adds a contents page, updates author/contact and keyword text, and corrects appendix cross-references, including 'Theorem 9' to 'Lemma 4' after Equation (97). The substantive prose and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: The manuscript receives a comprehensive visual redesign: branded title page, different typography and margins, colored headings and links, removed running headers, and widespread figure resizing and relocation. For example, Figures 11 and 12 now share a page; their scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: The contents page, additional project-page link, and repaired cross-references in Appendices A.3, A.5, and B.1 modestly improve navigation and traceability. The substantial visual redesign preserves the scientific material, while the theory, experiments, and findings remain unchanged. The supported overall gains are therefore limited.
